title: subscribe_events has no timeout — stream can hang indefinitely on server silence
description: client.rs subscribe_events: The HTTP GET request is sent without a timeout (no .timeout() call on the SSE request, unlike fetch_session/call/upload_blob/download_blob). This is intentional per the doc comment 'Does NOT apply to SSE or WebSocket streams (which are indefinite by nature)'. However, there is no heartbeat/ping detection and no idle timeout. A server that accepts the connection and then goes silent (e.g. a half-open TCP connection after a network partition) will hold the stream open indefinitely without yielding any frames. The caller has no way to distinguish a legitimately quiet server (no push events) from a dead connection. Maintenance consequence: users will file issues saying 'SSE stream stopped working after X minutes with no error'. Mitigation: document that callers must implement their own idle timeout using tokio::time::timeout on the stream. The doc comment for subscribe_events should state this explicitly.
